name: inputs
title: Inputs
about: Every way of answering a question: pick one; set a number on a slider, a dial, a keypad or as a pile you can count; put things in order; pair things by drawing strings, sorting them into bins or snapping jigsaw pieces together (or the old match); or tap the spot on a figure. It knows nothing about the question; a lesson says what to show and what counts as right. Every form answers, is checked, shows the truth and is recorded the same way.

form.about: Which way of answering. A number: slider, dial (the slider bent round a window), number (a keypad) or pile (a count you see at a glance). Pairs: string (draw a line to each partner), sort (drop things into bins), snap (jigsaw pieces into sockets); match is the old way, kept for old lessons.

options.about: The answers to pick from. Each has an id and its words.

shuffle.about: Mix the answers up each time, so their place gives nothing away. Order and snap always start out of order.

min.about: The low end of the scale. On a number, the lowest that can be typed. On a pile, the fewest it can hold (0 or more).

max.about: The high end of the scale. On a number, the highest that can be typed. On a pile, the most it can hold (up to 60).

step.about: What the value moves in: 1, 0.5, 0.1 and so on. A pile always counts in ones.

scale.about: Log stretches the scale, for answers that run over powers of ten. Needs min above 0.

unit.about: Shown after the value, like °C or km/h.

ticks.about: How many numbers to write along the scale.

start.about: Where it starts, with its fill showing: a real value, never a blank. Left out, the middle of the scale (a pile: its fewest). Keep it well away from the answer: a start inside the right band gives the answer away.

picture.about: A picture that follows the value: above a slider, in a dial's window. warmth: a ball that goes from a snowflake (low) to a fire (high), for temperature. depth: the sea cut away, with a warm layer as deep as the value. wind: a palm on an island, still at the low end, bent with its fronds streaming and the sea up in a gale at the high end.

pictureFrom.about: The value where the picture is at its low end (the snowflake; no warm layer; no wind). Left out, the low end of the scale.

pictureTo.about: The value where the picture is at its high end (the fire; the warm layer to the floor; a gale). Left out, the high end of the scale.

per.about: How many things to a row of the pile, so a count reads as rows: five unless the lesson says.

thing.about: What's piled: a plain dot, a hurricane seen from above, a drop of water, a leaf, a star or a coin.

thingImage.about: A picture from the topic to pile instead of a drawn thing: a path to a small, square picture.

items.about: The things to put in order, or to sort into bins. On a sort, each may have a small picture (image), and keep the words short: a bin is narrow.

ends.about: Words for the two ends of the order, like First and Last.

bins.about: The bins to sort into, side by side, each with its words and maybe a small picture (image). Any number of things can go in one bin.

left.about: The left column: on a snap, the cards with a socket. Each may have a small picture (image) beside its words.

right.about: The right column: on a snap, the pieces. Each left one pairs with exactly one of these; a snap has as many pieces as cards.

figure.about: The picture to tap on: a path to a picture in the topic. Left empty, a sample drawing.

aspect.about: The picture's height over its width, so the space is kept before it loads.

reveal.about: Shows the truth beside what was given: the right choice, the true value on the scale or dial, the true count on the pile, the right order, the right partners (gold strings, things hopping to their bins, pieces flying to their cards), the right spot.

mark.about: Colours the answer given on a slider, dial, number or pile: right, close or wrong.

lock.about: Stops any more changes, once an answer has been checked.

reset.about: Clears the answer and starts again.

value.about: choice: the id picked. slider, dial, number and pile: the number. order: the ids in order. string, snap and match: { leftId: rightId }. sort: { itemId: binId }. spot: { x, y } from 0 to 1 across and down the picture.

answered.about: Whether there is enough of an answer to check: something picked, a number typed, every left one paired, every thing sorted, every piece clicked in, a spot tapped. A slider, a dial, a pile and an order count as answered from the start: they always hold a real answer.

marking.about: How a Check step's answer becomes a rule (see docs/format.md). $answer is the step's answer, $within its tolerance, $close its wider tolerance for 'close'. Forms that answer alike are marked alike.

choice.answer: the id of the right option

order.answer: the ids in the right order

string.answer: { leftId: rightId } for every left one

match.answer: { leftId: rightId } for every left one

needs.weight: Light: a few dozen elements, small drawings, no canvas, nothing to download.
